We are building a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer- an interactive, educational simulator that replicates real-world space operations, problem-solving, and critical teamwork scenarios.
summary:
Sol Keeper: Mars Defender is a free browser game for kids aged 7 to 12 that works as a junior astronaut mission trainer. Players guard a Mars outpost for 10 sols (Mars days) and must share eight power units between Guns, Shield, Air and Food. Because power is limited, every choice has a cost. Spending more on guns means less for air, food or radiation protection.

The game turns real mission constraints into play. A message from Earth warns of a solar flare ahead of time, to show communication delay. Radiation can’t be shot, so only shielding protects the crew. Dust storms cut power, as on Mars. The flare is based on a real event in NASA’s DONKI database, the X9.3 flare of September 2017. The event timing is built into the game and is not fetched live.

It matters because children learn that deep-space survival is about balancing limited resources, not just having more of them. The game uses plain language, levels, pause and sound controls, and needs no download or account.
details:
What it does and how it works
Sol Keeper: Mars Defender is a free browser game for kids aged 7 to 12. Players guard a Mars outpost for 10 sols (Mars days), shooting falling rocks and collecting air, food and science supplies. Players have eight power units to share between four systems: Guns, Shield, Air and Food. Guns make shots stronger (a double shot at 3 units, a triple at 5), Shield blocks radiation, and Air and Food each need about 2 units to keep up. Players can change their power at any time, and every unit spent in one place is missing from another.

Real constraints it teaches
A message from Earth warns of a solar flare several seconds early, to show communication delay. Radiation can’t be shot, so only Shield power helps. Dust storms cut power from 8 to 4 units, as on Mars. The flare is based on a real event in NASA’s DONKI database, the X9.3 flare of 6 September 2017. The event timing is built into the game and is not fetched live.

Benefits and intended impact
Children learn that survival in deep space depends on balancing limited resources, not just having more of them. They practise planning ahead, weighing costs and reacting to warnings. The game needs no download or account, so it can be used at home or in a classroom.

Tools and technologies
HTML, CSS and JavaScript, drawn with the HTML5 Canvas, with sound from the Web Audio API and fonts from Google Fonts (Orbitron and Nunito). We used Claude, an AI assistant from Anthropic, to help write and refine the code. Hosting is a single web page, and it runs on phones and computers.

What is creative about it
We turned power budgeting, which is usually a spreadsheet task, into a fast arcade game. The trade-off is built into the controls, so players feel it while they play rather than reading about it. Astronaut characters, cheering pop-ups, levels and sound effects keep it fun.

Factors we considered

  • Kids’ needs: Plain language, short instructions, large buttons and a pause button with a 3-second countdown.
  • Difficulty: Every two sols is a new level, with only small increases in difficulty.
  • Accessibility: A mute button, and it needs no sign-up.
  • Honesty: Events are built in, and we plan to connect live DONKI data next.
